text:
sara: Quick follow-up from today's PM: recurring KV-cache OOM pattern still showing in prod clusters, creating this thread to track remediation owners and timelines.

jin: thanks. summary please — which clusters and which signal?

sara: prod-apac and prod-us-west. Pattern: background compaction + burst traffic => slab fragmentation spike => slow GC + growth in ghost allocations. Alerts: mem-residency > 85% for 10m then OOM within 30m.

rafi: noted. do we have a root cause PR or is this triage work?

ella: triage so far. we have a profiling trace from 2026-03-20 at 03:12Z showing repeated small live allocations pinned by long-lived handles. attaching snippet below.

ella: ```
# heap-prof summary
alloc_hotspots: kv_shard::insert_slice (45%)
retained_by: shard_map (holes)
fragmentation: slab-util down to 42%
concurrent-scan-latency: 120ms avg
```

marta: thanks. action proposals: 1) limit per-request temp allocations via pooled buffers 2) explicit soft limit + eviction for prefix-cache 3) GC pressure probe (force compaction) when slab-util < 50% and growth rate > 10%/5m

devon: +1 to pooled buffers. I can prototype buffer pool in runtime; estimate 3 days for a minimal patch + unit tests.

rafi: who owns the eviction policy changes? we need someone to own canary rollout and metrics.

marta: I'll own eviction policy changes and rollout. timeline: design review by 3/26, PR by 3/30, canary 4/2.

jin: what's the monitoring plan for canary? which metrics and thresholds?

marta: monitor: slab-util, mem-residency, eviction-rate, tail-latency p99. Canary alarms: mem-residency spike > 5% over baseline for 10m or p99 latency increase > 20%.

ops-bot: deploy reminder: canary will require coordination with infra (reserved nodes). Use #eng-infra to book.

rafa: (typo earlier) raf i -> rafi. btw, is there a light-weight GC forcing hook we can call opaquely?

ella: we have an internal endpoint: `POST /admin/compact?shard=<id>&mode=soft` — used in tests. Should document and add RBAC.

devon: prototype will use pooled buffers + expose an opt-in runtime flag `--pool-kv-bufs` guarded behind feature flag. I'll add telemetry counters: buf_allocs, buf_hits.

sara: sounds good. let's assign tickets: RT-4203 buffer pool; RT-4204 eviction policy + canary; RT-4205 admin compact endpoint RBAC + doc.

jin: do we need to update runbook for recurring incidents?

marta: yes. I'll update runbook to include: quick mitigation steps (trigger soft compact, toggle eviction aggressiveness, divert burst traffic to standby region), and triage checklist. ETA 3/28.

rafi: can we add a regression test in CI that simulates burst + compaction to catch this class?

ella: we have a sim harness. I'll add a regression job that runs weekly and fails on slab-util < 50% after synthetic burst. ETA 4/6.

devon: blockers: need perf infra access for nightly benchmarks to validate pooled buffers don't degrade p99. pinging @ops-bot to provision a perf cluster slot.

ops-bot: perf-cluster slot requested. ETA ~48h.

marta: risk note: aggressive eviction may impact cache hit-rate; we need side-by-side eval for cost vs latency. include cost impact estimate in PR description.

sara: outstanding owners & deadlines recap: devon (buffer pool prototype) 3d; marta (eviction + canary) design 3/26 PR 3/30 canary 4/2; ella (runbook + regression) 3/28 runbook, 4/6 regression job; rafi (CI test + validation) help on 4/6; ops-bot (perf slot) 48h.

jin: thanks — please add the RT tickets to the postmortem doc and link here when created.

marta: created RT-4204 (eviction) and RT-4205 (compact RBAC). will add links in the postmortem.

devon: created RT-4203 (buffer pool) and pushed a WIP branch: `feature/pool-kv-bufs`. PTAL @ella @marta.

ella: reviewing now. quick ask: add a small benchmark harness in repo to reproduce allocation churn; attach script and run instructions in PR.

rafi: i'll own postmortem follow-through tracking: I'll run weekly checkins until all tickets closed, and put a short status note in the memory backlog doc.

sara: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll reconvene next Friday for status. :thumbsup:
